approach.method_basis: The failed NF-BO Parent searches around already scored molecules using an injective SELFIES sequence flow. It learns the flow density from unlabeled molecules, adapts the same flow to high-scoring observations within each independent objective, and re-encodes every observation before fitting its latent Gaussian process. It generates fresh trust-region proposals by perturbing whole token blocks according to estimated sequence-level pointwise mutual information, ranks them with correlated Thompson samples, and decodes through the explicit inverse flow. Canonical validity and novelty checks refill each announced batch. This recovery retains that algorithm and every bound mechanism.
approach.novelty: This is a numerical recovery of the failed Parent, not a new research mechanism. Execute the loaded task-local flow, recurrent states, and its continuous latent path in double precision so that rounding drift is less likely to cross a token-decoding boundary after adaptation. Preserve the strict equality check for every token, including termination and padding, and retain every adaptation step. The proposed precision repair is not yet verified; success requires the original reconstruction checks and complete task execution.

observed_bottleneck: The single recorded failure in Parent n-77c41c9bc036 is a crash at the strict sequence-flow left-inverse assertion immediately after task-local adaptation. Its seed-0 summary records drd2_docking stopping at 150 oracle calls and median_2 at 240. The corresponding candidate stderr records 149/150 and 239/240 exact padded-token reconstructions, although every canonical molecular identity still matches. Maximum continuous inverse error grows from about 5.36e-7 at initialization to 0.295334 and 0.308024 before the failing updates, then 0.405526 and 0.404005 afterward; minimum embedding separation remains 0.754210. The source computes the forward recurrent conditioner over a whole sequence and its inverse one reconstructed token at a time in float32. These records support accumulated finite-precision inverse drift as the repair hypothesis, but do not isolate the mismatched token positions or establish that they are padding. The preparation and three other objective sessions complete; novelty exhaustion, wrong batch size, and posterior calibration are not the recorded crash.
hypothesis: Recover the recorded post-adaptation left-inverse crash by promoting the loaded task-local sequence flow and its continuous recurrent forward/inverse latent calculations from float32 to float64, with dtype-compatible probe assignment and unchanged strict token reconstruction checks.

finding_summary.headline: Double precision restores exact reconstruction and completes all five tasks; recorded best scores stay unchanged.
finding_summary.insights: The result supports finite-precision recurrent inverse drift as a recoverable implementation bottleneck: strict equality survives without omitting padding, dropping observations, or skipping adaptation. It does not identify the original mismatched token positions, so a padding-only explanation remains unproven. Numerical recovery also leaves the main search-quality questions intact. Nominal 95% GP intervals cover only 466 of 1,450 outcomes (32.1%); coverage on the 1,240 shared predictions is unchanged at 444 outcomes, and only 22 of the 210 added predictions are covered. In addition, 97.6% of examined decodes reproduce their generating center. The molecular assessment finds the same narrow high-scoring families and recurring unusual charged heteroatoms and chain growth, with weak chemical plausibility. These findings make surrogate calibration and useful, chemically credible local variation worth probing independently. Recovery is demonstrated for this seed and checkpoint under the existing budget; continuous inverse error still reaches 0.004864 in one successful check, so exact reconstruction here does not establish stability for arbitrary future histories.
finding_summary.results: On the screening seed, all five objectives complete 300 evaluations. The two sessions that previously stopped at 150 and 240 evaluations now finish, bringing the total from 1,290 to 1,500. All 300 reconstruction checks preserve the full padded token sequence and canonical molecule: 46,500 of 46,500 observation-check instances match exactly. At the former failure points, maximum continuous inverse error falls from 0.405526 to 0.000005301 on drd2_docking and from 0.404005 to 0.00000001510 on median_2. Preparation produces the identical checkpoint. All 150 online adaptations execute their original 24 steps, every GP fit uses freshly encoded observations, PMI still favors informative token blocks, and posterior uncertainty still affects selection. Every emitted batch contains ten valid novel molecules. The completed macro score is 0.419751565. All 1,290 shared trajectory records match the parent exactly, and the additional 210 evaluations produce no new task best. Because the parent lacks a complete macro score, these results establish numerical recovery without establishing a paired macro-score gain.

molecular.headline: Recognizable aryl and nitrogen heterocycles persist among the high scorers, amid unusual charged heteroatoms and unsaturated chains.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-50bccbe8104b produces recognizable aryl amides, diaryl nitrogen linkers, pyrrolidines and carbonyl-rich heterocycles, together with extensive ring opening, unusual heteroatom substitutions and chain growth. The seed-0 digest covers 300 records per task, including 290 optimizer proposals and 10 supplied initial molecules. Rings are frequent: the per-task ring-closure rates range from 0.631 to 0.9828, while aromatic-marker rates range from 0.3103 to 0.6517. These are fractions of SMILES containing text markers, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. The output is therefore neither ring-free nor uniformly aromatic. Its most recognizable higher-scoring series remain concentrated around a few aryl and nitrogen-containing frameworks, despite 300 unique recorded molecules per task. The collection has weak medicinal-chemistry plausibility because ordinary fragments are repeatedly connected through undercoordinated charged atoms, unusual multiply bonded boron, phosphorus or sulfur, labile-looking nitrogen/oxygen linkages, or long unsaturated tails. The synthetic-plausibility judgment concerns these specific combinations; it does not assert that all organoboron, organophosphorus, charged molecules or cumulenes are impossible. No synthesis or stability evidence is supplied, and no measured binding interpretation is inferred from a scalar score. Compared with Parent n-77c41c9bc036, every shared trajectory record is identical in molecule, score and evaluation order. Three full trajectories are unchanged; the other two extend identical prefixes from 150 and 240 records to 300. Every task retains the same recorded best score. The added chemistry continues the same structural families and liabilities. All score-gradient readings below describe associations within these supplied molecules, without assigning unseen objective requirements.

per_task.generated_character: The recognizable higher-scoring molecules are medium-sized pyrrole or indole carboxanilides carrying methoxy/enol-ether substituents and a fluorophenyl or phosphorus-substituted phenyl group. The initial molecule at evaluation 9 is a conventional trimethoxyindole carboxanilide; evaluation 247 retains a pyrrole carboxanilide but carries an unsaturated tail containing cationic phosphorus and an imine. Other high examples include the small annulated ring at evaluation 121. Lower-scoring output often replaces the aromatic framework with long alkyl/polyene chains and unusual boron, sulfur and charged oxygen motifs. Mean SMILES length is 47.8 characters and the maximum is 239; these describe textual size, not molecular weight. The optimizer-only ring, aromatic, charged and cumulated-double-bond marker rates are 0.8207, 0.5, 0.4828 and 0.4207. This entire trajectory matches the Parent.
liabilities: Undercoordinated phosphorus ions, unusual boron cumulenes and selenium-containing termini make many proposed complete structures difficult to regard as routine isolable compounds.
The 239-character proposal contains a long repeated phosphorus-cation chain; chain growth can overwhelm an otherwise recognizable aromatic amide.
Enol ethers, imines and small annulated unsaturated rings introduce stability or strain questions that the recorded score does not resolve.
missing_features: Reliable preservation of the aromatic carboxanilide framework across peripheral changes; much of the low-scoring output loses that arrangement.

A broad series of compact, conventionally bonded substituents that explores the higher-scoring core without unusual phosphorus, boron or selenium termini. Such a series is not demonstrated by the cited high examples.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145; the phosphorus-bearing pyrrole derivative at evaluation 247 scores 0.3589400387570429. The neutral annulated derivative at evaluation 121 scores 0.32669259058368827. Retention of the aromatic carboxanilide arrangement is associated with these higher values, whereas the long nonaromatic boron/polyene structure at evaluation 260 scores 3.4534272407390813e-25. Merely retaining the core is insufficient: the very long phosphorus-cation chain appended at evaluation 295 scores 2.5818561705812328e-20. Evaluations 27 and 34 have exactly the same score, 0.3012013878124864, despite replacing aryl fluorine with an anionic phosphorus atom. The observed gradient therefore does not establish a benefit from that phosphorus substitution or a requirement for fluorine. The final molecule scores 0.20011411946944202 and still carries the core with a selenium/charged-oxygen tail.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring set contains medium-sized diaryl structures with methoxy substituents, a fluorinated aniline ring, and a tetrahedral carbon bearing a methyl group, hydroxyl and two nitrogen substituents. Evaluation 85 joins the aryl groups through an ether-containing nitrogen linker; evaluation 13 is a cyclized diaryl congener. These retain more ordinary carbon, nitrogen and oxygen connectivity than the conspicuous exotic structures on the other trajectories, although the hydroxylated gem-diamine center raises a stability question. An anionic aromatic boron variant appears at evaluation 286. The low end includes fluoromethane and small unsaturated fragments; late molecules often lose both aryl rings and carry carbanions, alkynes, sulfur or cyclopropenes. Mean SMILES length is 40.4 characters and the maximum is 61. Ring, aromatic, charged and cumulated-double-bond marker rates are 0.7862, 0.5759, 0.2966 and 0.1276. This entire trajectory matches the Parent.
liabilities: A carbon bearing hydroxyl and two nitrogen substituents is an unusual carbinolamine/aminal-like center whose hydrolytic and configurational stability is untested.
The high aromatic-boron variant and late carbanions require more chemical justification than formal SMILES validity.
Late alkynes, cumulated bonds and small unsaturated rings frequently accompany loss of the recognizable aryl framework; potentially stereogenic centers remain unspecified.
missing_features: Consistent retention of the decorated diaryl arrangement during linker exploration; tiny fragments and the final aryl-free chains lack features shared by the high examples.

Demonstrated stable alternatives to the hydroxylated gem-diamine linkage that preserve its aryl spacing and nitrogen/oxygen functionality. The score data do not establish whether any particular replacement would be rewarded.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied initial carbonyl-rich heterocycle at evaluation 7 scores 0.548381482770623. The diaryl hydroxylated gem-diamines at evaluations 85 and 13 score 0.5748346675948486 and 0.5710412519733681. Fluoromethane at evaluation 96 and the small fluorinated allene/alkyne at evaluation 166 both score the observed floor of 0.5. Within this narrow score span, retaining decorated aryl groups and the nitrogen/oxygen linker is associated with higher values than fragmenting the molecule. The aromatic boron variant scores 0.568883762655389, so an unusual element substitution is tolerated among high values without exceeding the ordinary-carbon best example. The late aryl-free carbanion at evaluation 295 scores 0.5038648836670017, and the final unsaturated aminal-like structure scores 0.5195058517555267. These observations do not isolate a required linker geometry or establish that the hydroxylated center is chemically stable.

per_task.generated_character: The high examples are large, branched, multiply cyclic structures retaining fluoromethoxyaryl and dichloroaryl groups, a pyrrolidine, a primary amine, a carboxylic acid and a carbonyl. They also contain an unusual macrocyclic connection through carbon triple-bonded to cationic sulfur and an anionic boron/nitrogen segment. Evaluation 91 substitutes aromatic phosphorus into an aryl ring; evaluation 223 replaces a hydroxyl with a thiol on that same broad framework. A potentially basic saturated ring nitrogen is already present, so absence of ring amines would be an incorrect diagnosis. Mean SMILES length is 76.5 characters and the maximum is 97. Ring, aromatic, charged and halogen marker rates are 0.9828, 0.3345, 0.931 and 0.9931. Thus frequent ring closures often describe nonaromatic, chemically unusual rings. The continuation after the identical 150-record Parent prefix retains this chemistry through evaluation 300.
liabilities: A carbon-sulfur triple bond at a multiply connected cationic sulfur, combined with anionic boron/nitrogen segments, creates severe questions about chemical stability and preparative plausibility.
Aromatic phosphorus, charged selenium/oxygen variants and mixed formal charges appear among high examples; a high scalar score supplies no synthesis or protonation-state validation.
Late strained unsaturated rings and enlarged aliphatic connections add complexity while often dismantling the decorated aryl regions.
missing_features: Chemically credible complete structures that retain the high examples' decorated aryl groups, saturated ring nitrogen and polar side chain while using conventional connecting bonds.
Reliable preservation of aromatic surfaces within this framework; many lower-scoring molecules keep ring closures but replace the aryl groups with extended nonaromatic chains.
Specified stereochemistry for the substituted pyrrolidine and amino-bearing carbon. The trajectories do not establish a preferred stereoisomer.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl amide/sulfonamide at evaluation 10 scores 0.01904115112334333. Evaluations 80, 91 and 223 all score 0.6518038575322768 despite changes to aromatic carbon/phosphorus and hydroxyl/thiol substitution. The related open-chain analogue retaining both decorated aryl groups and the amino-acid/pyrrolidine region at evaluation 282 scores 0.5553249468028342. The much smaller dichloroaryl boron/nitrile fragment at evaluation 75 scores 0.0019425392934534736; the small nonaromatic final-band structure at evaluation 296 scores 0.005130987211464107. This associates the more complete aryl/polar framework with higher recorded values, while giving no independent evidence that the unusual sulfur or boron bonding causes a useful molecular interaction. The conventional initial ring-amine molecule at evaluation 6 has the overall minimum, 0.0003786988088202195, so a ring amine alone is insufficient. The added trajectory ties the Parent best at evaluation 223; the final molecule scores 0.025522236148142387.

per_task.generated_character: The recognizable series comprises medium-to-large molecules with a hydroxybenzoate ethyl ester, a phenyl group and a fused or rearranged nitrogen heterocycle carrying N-methyl carbonyl groups. The supplied initial molecule at evaluation 7 is an aromatic pyrrole/pyrimidinedione framework. The best generated molecule at evaluation 93 retains its aryl and dicarbonyl features but inserts multicoordinate hydrogen-bearing sulfur into the fused ring system; evaluation 124 has further sulfur substitution. Evaluation 80 demonstrates a rearranged nitrogen/carbon framework with conventional ester and carbonyl groups. Lower-scoring molecules include long polyenes ending in a thioformate or phosphorus-containing carbonyl chain. Mean SMILES length is 55.1 characters and the maximum is 72. Ring, aromatic and charged marker rates are 0.9724, 0.6517 and 0.5483. The extension beyond the identical 240-record Parent prefix continues ring rearrangement, sulfur/phosphorus substitution and aromatic loss.
liabilities: Hydrogen-bearing sulfur atoms bonded into several ring positions have unusual coordination; their apparent validity does not establish an accessible stable compound.
Boron-carbon triple-bond motifs and charged phosphorus/carbonyl chains recur alongside otherwise familiar ester and imide fragments.
Conjugated chains and newly rearranged rings often have unspecified geometry or stereochemistry, and their synthetic routes are not demonstrated.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of both aryl substitution patterns and the nitrogen/carbonyl heterocycle; low-scoring chain products omit substantial portions of that arrangement.

Broader exploration of ordinary ester, amide and heterocycle changes around the near-best initial scaffold. High examples remain a closely related series, often with unusual ring sulfur or boron substitution.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best generated sulfur-containing fused heterocycle scores 0.17106143261991325, close to the initial aromatic dicarbonyl framework at 0.1678386594791329. The further sulfur variant scores 0.16458734630954286, and the conventionally bonded rearranged nitrogen heterocycle at evaluation 80 scores 0.15961077554209194. Replacing the initial ethoxy ester linkage with the unusual boron/alkyne segment at evaluation 21 yields 0.15463842820677165. These comparisons support retaining the aryl and nitrogen/carbonyl arrangement, without establishing an advantage for exotic heteroatoms as a class. The ring-free polyene thioformate at evaluation 44 scores 0.009273980187776159, and its phosphorus-containing low-scoring relative at evaluation 73 scores 0.012659242088545842. The final partly ring-retaining polyene/boron structure scores 0.07866459694094406. The continuation supplies no new recorded best molecule beyond the Parent.

per_task.generated_character: The high generated series centers on a pyrrole carboxamide with a methoxy-substituted boron-ended cumulene, a vinyl-alcohol substituent and an unsaturated amide side chain containing phosphorus, sometimes fluorine or sulfur. These are medium-sized strings with recognizable pyrrole/amide functionality but strongly unusual peripheral bonding. Evaluation 196 is the best example; evaluation 112 extends the unusual bonding into a boron/phosphorus cumulene. The initial indole carboxanilide at evaluation 9 is a more conventional member of the same broad nitrogen-aromatic/amide chemistry. Lower-scoring and late output frequently loses the aromatic pyrrole and grows nonaromatic boron/phosphorus chains. Mean SMILES length is 41.4 characters and the maximum is 158. Ring, aromatic, charged and cumulated-double-bond marker rates are 0.631, 0.3103, 0.3552 and 0.9483. This is extensive unsaturated heteroatom-chain chemistry, with aromaticity confined to part of the set. The entire trajectory matches the Parent.
liabilities: Boron-ended cumulenes, multiply bonded phosphorus and hydrogen-bearing sulfur combinations dominate the recognizable high series and pose substantial synthetic-plausibility questions.
Vinyl-alcohol and imine-like or other unsaturated heteroatom motifs can have alternative chemical forms whose stability is not addressed by the trajectory.
The 158-character zero-scoring molecule contains repeated phosphorus-cation and nitrogen-chain segments, illustrating severe chain-growth and charge liabilities.
missing_features: Reliable preservation of the substituted aromatic pyrrole and its carboxamide; most late examples lack that complete combination.

A demonstrated series of conventionally bonded, isolable alternatives to the boron/phosphorus cumulene and unsaturated side chains while retaining the useful core. Its score consequences remain untested in the shown comparison.
Defined alkene geometry and chemically resolved enol-containing forms for the high examples; the recorded SMILES leave these aspects of molecular identity unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxanilide scores 0.00012094961439027578. The boron/phosphorus-containing pyrrole amides at evaluations 196, 80 and 112 score 0.34211782765871057, 0.3240344860672695 and 0.29915901510860066. A related pyrrole amide with a sulfur-containing cyclic side group at evaluation 29 scores 0.25194110074598225. These higher values are associated with the substituted pyrrole/amide arrangement and its particular unsaturated substituents; the available molecules do not separate each substituent's contribution. A long phosphorus-cation/nitrogen-chain structure at evaluation 85 scores 0.0. The small ring-free boron cumulene at evaluation 297 scores 6.544064713837032e-12, and the nonaromatic phosphorus/boron heterocycle retaining an amide at evaluation 298 scores 4.30443081853892e-14. Thus a cumulene or amide alone does not account for the high values. The final molecule scores 4.130208343349009e-09. The score span does not demonstrate that the high structures are stable or that a particular unobserved medicinal-chemistry motif is required.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Higher-scoring examples repeatedly retain a pyrrole carboxamide, decorated diaryl nitrogen linker, aryl/pyrrolidine combination or phenyl dicarbonyl heterocycle. Low and final examples often convert their rings into polyenes or remove the amide, ester or aryl context while retaining only isolated fragments.
transferable_gaps.gap: Peripheral diversification does not reliably preserve the intact aromatic and polar frameworks associated with higher observed scores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically local substituent and bond changes that can preserve complete ring and functional-group arrangements. Let accepted task-local score responses determine which arrangements are retained and when coherent scaffold changes are explored.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest contains terminal multiply bonded boron, undercoordinated phosphorus cations, carbon triple-bonded to multiply connected cationic sulfur, unusual ring sulfur and aromatic phosphorus. Charged-marker rates range from 0.2966 to 0.931. Even the more conventional diaryl series concentrates on a hydroxylated gem-diamine whose stability is untested.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks dependable chemical control over element coordination, charge context and stable functional-group combinations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make chemically supported local coordination and functional-group contexts available during generation, including ordinary amine, ether, amide and carbonyl connectivity. Assess the complete bonding and charge pattern when exploring less common elements, using the same chemical criteria for every objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The recorded output includes fluoromethane at the observed 0.5 floor, long ring-free polyenes at very low scores, a 239-character phosphorus-cation-chain proposal scoring 2.5818561705812328e-20, and a 158-character repeated phosphorus/nitrogen-chain proposal scoring 0.0.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably keep molecular size and chain continuation within a coherent small-molecule structure.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support controlled termination, side-chain length and chemically coherent closure so diversification can retain an existing molecular framework without collapsing into tiny fragments or appending repetitive charged chains. Use general molecular context and allowed feedback to determine useful size variation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each task contains 290 distinct optimizer proposals, yet the high-scoring excerpts repeatedly revisit closely related aryl/nitrogen frameworks. Much of the wider visible variation consists of ring opening, unsaturated-chain growth or unusual element replacement. The added trajectories continue the same families and retain the Parent's recorded best scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator shows narrow diversity among chemically recognizable high-scoring frameworks despite many unique strings.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand access to coherent alternative ring systems and conventional linker arrangements that preserve relevant polar and aromatic features. Use current observations to explore their utility without hard-coded target identities or target-specific functional-group requirements.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0 in the optimizer-only digest. The shown molecules nevertheless include asymmetric amino-bearing carbons, substituted saturated nitrogen rings, hydroxylated gem-diamine centers and unsaturated side chains without specified configurations or alkene geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Potentially stereogenic and geometrically distinct generated structures are not represented as fully specified chemical identities.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support chemically valid stereochemical and geometric specification when those features arise, preserving specified identities through proposal generation. Determine whether resolved alternatives matter through ordinary task-local feedback; the present scores do not identify a preferred stereoisomer.

method_name: NF-BO: invertible sequence-flow search with token-adaptive latent proposals
method_thesis: Use NF-BO's SeqFlow mapping, exact left-inverse decoding, and token-adaptive trust-region search. Train a compact SELFIES flow on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Within each fresh objective session, adapt it using highly scored task-local sequences, re-encode all observations after updates, and fit a latent-space GP. Generate new latent proposals around scored observations by perturbing token blocks according to their estimated pointwise mutual information with the decoded sequence. Thompson sampling selects proposals for inverse-flow decoding. These mechanisms follow [NF-BO, Sections 4 and 5.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.14889v1). Regenerate as needed to fill the evaluator-announced batch with distinct canonical molecules; no corpus molecules are ranked or retrieved. The hypothesis is that score-directed local search around exactly reconstructable observations finds improving structures efficiently enough to raise the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Exact reconstruction alone is not the objective. Useful flow training and surrogate prediction under the permitted preparation and feedback remain empirical prerequisites.
